successors.name: Kahuripan
successors.text: East Java: 'Airlangga ... re-established the kingdom ... under the name of kingdom of Kahuripan in 1019'

ledger.x: c. 717: Sanjaya comes to power in Central Java. 'It seemed that Sanjaya came to power c. 717 AD'; the earliest account of the kingdom is the Canggal inscription of 732, and the Sanjaya page gives 716 (Damais) and the reign as 716-746 or 732-760.
c. 929: the court goes to East Java. 'Around the year 929, the centre of the kingdom was shifted from Central Java to East Java by Mpu Sindok'; Tamwlang and Watugaluh become the seats.
c. 929: Mpu Sindok founds the Isyana dynasty in East Java. The page names him 'founder of the Isyana dynasty'; the kingdom, its colour and the East Java land continue (rule 2).

c. 990: Bali becomes Mataram's vassal, probably. Bali 'probably was an ally or vassal of Java' in the 11th century; the marriage of Mahendradatta, Dharmawangsa's sister, to Udayana was 'probably... a political means to seal Bali as part of Mataram's realm'. The page dates neither; the Mataram page has Bali 'probably'…
1016: Mataram falls and Bali is on its own.

wars.name: Sanjaya's invasion of Galuh
wars.outcome: Purbasora killed in 723; Premanadikusuma installed; Galuh under Mataram influence until Manarah's revolt of 739.

wars.name: Mataram-Srivijayan wars
wars.outcome: No land changes hands: the Anjukladang inscription of 937 'mentions an infiltration attack from Malayu'; 'In 990, King Dharmawangsa of Java launched a naval invasion against Srivijaya'; in 1006 Srivijaya repelled the Javanese invasion; the infobox gives 'c.

wars.name: Wurawari revolt against Dharmawangsa
wars.outcome: Dharmawangsa killed and the capital destroyed (the 'Pralaya of Mataram'); Airlangga escapes and founds Kahuripan in 1019.

certainty.note: The inscriptions give centres and rulers, never frontiers; the East Java reach is from the Balitung description only.
